pairs.subject: usage-limit-governance
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 admits against terminal-status-only spend (src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2346) read before the insert, so queued/running runs are invisible and a burst overshoots by up to N budgets; src-tauri/engine/src/http_engine/openai.rs:232 stamps unpriced remote models $0.0, so that traffic spends against the cap for free (re-confirmed; openai.rs anchor moved from src-tauri/src/engine/)

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:472 get_monthly_spend is a check-then-act read with no per-persona exclusive section, and the predicate at src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2346 excludes queued/running rows - concurrent launches all pass on pre-burst spend

src-tauri/engine/src/http_engine/openai.rs:232 None => 0.0 (and src-tauri/engine/src/http_engine/config.rs:44 cost_of) writes unpriced spend as zero instead of null+imputation; the enforcing cap reads it as headroom and never refuses as unmeasurable

src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:470 cost metric x UTC calendar-month window x max_budget_usd threshold x hard-stop action; budget>0 guard treats non-positive as no cap rather than rejecting at write time; no observe-only or soft-warning tier on the local cap
src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 single >= wall, no ramp - acceptable for a per-persona monthly cap with low event rate, not counted toward the deviation

pairs.registryProposal: Boundary question: the golden path places a program capping its OWN emitted traffic on the builder side, outside this subject; Personas caps the runs it itself launches, so this pair may be a technique-shaped resonance (concurrent-admission-integrity and cost-evidence-and-imputation apply regardless). The registry should say whether a local-first multi-agent runner capping per-agent spend is governed here or by cost-metering, so the six consumer deviations it ranks on are not partly a routing artifact.
